object_description: layered volume with a flying pavilion of classrooms over an open ground floor
design_condition: the building is placed on the north-western edge of the site, leaving a spacious surrounding area for the neighbouring estates and creating a relaxed situation that benefits the whole neighbourhood

positive: The placement gives the adjacent estates a spacious surrounding area and a spatially relaxed situation
The school is simply divided into three functionally separate horizontal layers
The ground floor holds gymnasium, pool and other uses accessible to the neighbourhood
The unexpected and interesting gesture of the open gym was impressive
All classrooms are organised on one level in the flying pavilion with the ancillary rooms
The spacious layout offers great flexibility for possible conversions
Its carpet-like floor plan pattern recalls Nordic school building examples
The structural design is logical and corresponds to the clear layered section
Large floor-to-ceiling steel girders span the lowered gymnasium and pool and carry the curved shed roofs
Escape routes on the upper floor are organised via external walkways and stairs
The building volume is fundamentally compact
The open space stays visually permeable from the park despite the placement
Groups of trees and fine terrain modelling can create a connecting green band with neighbourhood park character
The park-like green areas provide adequate space for a lawn and a public playground
The all-weather area with parking, bicycle parking and recreation is sensibly positioned
The open forecourt and the south-eastern playground with the central green area are appropriately designed
The choice and placement of trees creates an independent atmosphere corresponding to the park context
The approach impresses with its potential to create a neighbourhood centre
It gives a clear architectural formulation of a building for a contemporary, communal school
negative: The placement slightly restricts the flowing green space towards the neighbouring development
The open gym still needs to be optimised for everyday use
The inner classrooms lit only by the four atriums lack an outdoor connection
The planned sheds and the materialisation with a large proportion of glass may be costly
A more precise interplay of density and expanse in the tree placement is desirable for zoning and opening
The school garden is somewhat cramped in the terraced area and needs review
